text:
Alex R.: Quick async standup — what I did / blockers / today

What I did: rolled kv-evict fix to 10% canary on batcher pool, validated warm-up path, re-ran synthetic for long-seq throughput. Metrics look better for small requests.
Blockers: seeing intermittent 504s on /v1/generate for requests > 1024 tokens during short bursts. Stack traces point to queue backpressure + occasional serializing pauses.
Today: bump batcher concurrency by 2, push rate-limit fallback on heavy routes, and open a PR for a short TTL on cold-KV entries. Asking for a quick CR: @Raj P. can you take a look when you have a minute? Also tagging @Maria C. in case the evening oncall needs context.

Logs snippet I used:
```bash
# find recent 504s on batcher
kubectl logs deploy/batcher -n prod | grep '504' | tail -n 40
```

Maria C.: saw the alert at 03:18 — thanks for pushing the canary. Two quick notes: 1) autoscaler cooldown was 120s for that pool yesterday, might be too slow for bursty traffic. 2) heap/GC spikes on that node correlated with request bursts in grafana. If you want I can drop the cooldown to 60s for the canary group for the next 6 hours. :thumbsup:

Raj P.: I'll review the PR (alex/kv-ttl-rate-limit) tonight — ETA 2h. Quick Q: what's the expected peak QPS on the canary right now? I want to ensure my change doesn't reduce headroom. Also +1 on a short token-bucket per-route limiter rather than global, less risky.

Alex R.: good call. Canary QPS ~ 120p50 bursts to 280 over 30s. The short limiter plan is per-route (heavy routes only) with a fallback to a lighter model variant. Putting the PR link here: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/4821. I added a short doc in the PR description about the fallback policy.

Jin S.: added a quick dashboard panel (embed) to the PR comments — looks like p95 latency and queue depth spike at the same times as the 504s: https://grafana.redwood/board/ops/canary-batcher. Also experimented with soft-KV evict: evict idle keys < 60s to reduce memory pressure; CPU impact negligible. Suggest testing that on the canary only.

sre-bot: Alert suppressed: GPU-alloc-high for batcher-pool-7 — suppression set for 30m based on ongoing canary.

Maria C.: I'll take the night oncall handoff for 18:00–06:00. If the 504 noise rises after you bump concurrency, ping #incidents and I'll escalate. I can drop the autoscaler cooldown for the canary temporarily; Alex, say the word and I'll run the change.

Alex R.: please do, Maria — set cooldown to 60s for the canary pool and keep suppression window. I'll push the concurrency bump + the short limiter PR in the next 20m. Thanks all. :pray: 

Raj P.: noted, I'll review and comment inline. If tests pass, we can roll to 30% after a 45m observation window.

Jin S.: leaving a tiny runbook note in the PR for oncall: what to watch (p95 > 800ms, queue depth > 50, 504 count > 5/min) and the rollback steps.

sre-bot: Deployment started: batcher-concurrency-bump (canary) by alex — build 7745.

oncall-scheduler: Reminder — Maria C. is oncall tonight 18:00-06:00 (UTC). Use @Maria C. in-channel for paging.

Alex R.: closing loop — will post a short follow-up in 45m with observation summary.

(footnote: lightweight thread — keeping replies concise so oncall can scan quickly)
